title: Modi Calls for Global Tech Rules, Origin Tracking for Deepfakes and AI Content
key_facts: Narendra Modi called for 'global standards and common rules for emerging technologies' in a PIB release dated 6 Oct 2026.
He suggested exploring ways for users to identify the origin of deepfakes and AI-generated content immediately.
He spoke to GSMA board members, the global body of mobile operators, in Delhi.
He also urged technology-driven solutions to cyber fraud and affordable digital services for the Global South.
India's February 2026 IT Rules amendments already require platforms with AI content tools to embed permanent provenance metadata 'to the extent technically feasible'.
The PIB release does not say whether 'origin' means the tool or the person who created the content; India has no dedicated AI law.
quote_evidence: Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for "global standards and common rules for emerging technologies" and suggested exploring mechanisms that would let users immediately identify the origin of deepfakes and AI-generated content, according to a Press Information Bureau (PIB) release on October 6.
The PIB release does not say whether "origin" means the tool or the person who created the content.
why_it_matters_hint: India's leader backs global rules and clear labelling of AI content; naming the person behind content would raise old privacy and encryption disputes.
notes: Based on an official PIB release and Modi's X post, as reported by MediaNama.
